stem: A 30 kg child can take oral medication and needs an analgesic dose from the emergency drug table; which option matches oral oxycodone?
explanation: Oral oxycodone is the correct answer. The emergency drug table lists oxycodone as 0.1 mg/kg by mouth for analgesia.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 147

optionExplanations.A: Correct because oral oxycodone is listed at 0.1 mg/kg.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 0.05–0.1 mg/kg IV is the morphine dose range, not oral oxycodone.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 1.5 micrograms/kg intranasal is the fentanyl dose, not oxycodone.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 10 micrograms/kg IV is the adrenaline dose used in cardiac arrest, not oxycodone.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 0.15 mg/kg IV or IM is a benzodiazepine dose used for seizures, not oral oxycodone.
